answer: At the zenith of the network, each AI agent locks a stake token into a vault that assigns quadratic weight: one long‑standing identity counts fully, while the combined influence of many fresh IDs grows only as the square‑root of their total stake. New agents must first earn reputation in the ocean of tasks, paying micro‑fees that accumulate; to gain a linear share they need to reach a threshold, so an attacker must spend the square of the desired influence, rendering Sybil floods financially infeasible.
